newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BROLIN SET FOR LEEDS RETURN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BROLIN SET FOR LEEDS RETURN.

text.p: Swedish international Tomas Brolin has agreed to return to England for peace talks with Leeds United, his Swiss side FC Zurich said on Tuesday.
Brolin, who fell out with former Leeds boss Howard Wilkinson, had defied demands from injury-hit United to return from the Swiss club, where he has been on loan for a month.
In retaliation, Leeds refused to extend the loan period, stopped Brolin's wages and threatened to press for a worldwide ban on the player.
Leeds, now under the guidance of ex-Arsenal manager George Graham, appear to have finally achieved their goal.
"Tomas trained with us today but he has told me he plans to fly back to Leeds and I'm sure he will arrive in the next few days," FC Zurich secretary Eric Schmid said.

Graham wants Brolin back to ease an injury crisis that has robbed last season's League Cup finalists of four strikers -- Ghanaian Tony Yeboah, Welshman Ian Rush, Brian Deane and former England striker Mark Hateley.
Brolin joined Leeds from Parma nearly a year ago for 4.5 million pounds ($7 million), but was unhappy at failing to win a regular first team place under Wilkinson.
Graham, who took over from Wilkinson at Elland Road last month, has promised him a fresh start.
